code.note: Unzip 903.zip in an empty directory. Build with gfortran (the package's Makefile uses g95; the rerun records the compiler used) the sources frb_step.f and driver_example0.f, run from Fortran77/Drivers so that init_example0.dat is read, and compare the written out_example0.dat with the shipped copy.

field: mechanics / numerics (free rigid body, geometric integration)

claim.location: Shipped reference output Fortran77/Drivers/out_example0.dat (inside 903.zip), line 14: the output angular momentum component PIOUT(1) after one step. The driver computes one exact (Np = 0) step of length h = 0.1 for the free rigid body with inertia (1.0, 1.6487857827119290, 1.9720127096641928) from init_example0.dat, using frb_step.f.

reference.sha256: not computed for the member; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.paper_value: Value -0.7088447919224319 at line 14 of the shipped out_example0.dat, as written by the shipped driver (16 significant digits). The paper's table or figure is not read; the claim is the code's own printed output.
claim.metric: Line 14 of the regenerated out_example0.dat (first component of the output angular momentum after one step), compared as an absolute number with the shipped value
claim.determinism: deterministic (fixed init_example0.dat input, no random numbers, Np = 0 exact elliptic integration)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference holds 16 significant digits of a double-precision computation, so rounding is about 1e-16. 1e-10 leaves room for compiler and libm differences in the elliptic-integral evaluation and the sqrt normalisation, which in double precision are typically 1e-14 to 1e-12. A sign error, an inertia-index swap or a wrong step size moves this component by about 1e-3 or more at h = 0.1, so the tolerance cannot hide those. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 2 minutes: one gfortran build of two source files and one driver run; the shipped driver does a single step.
cost.data_size: None (init_example0.dat is 6 lines inside the archive).
cost.data_licence: Netlib CALGO archive; licence per the archive's own notices and 903.head (the rerun should record it).

why: The shipped driver evaluates one step of the free rigid body equations, with the elliptic integrals of the exact solution; the value at line 14 is a numerical evaluation with no closed form, so the rerun must execute the Fortran method to reproduce it.
